name: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation — National Rates and Rate Caps
description: The FDIC's monthly national average deposit rates and interest-rate caps for savings, interest checking, money market and certificate-of-deposit accounts, calculated from bank- and credit-union-level data and used to cap the rates a less-than-well-capitalized institution may offer.

notes: The current-month page (https://www.fdic.gov/national-rates-and-rate-caps) is an HTML table only, no file link. Historical data is two downloadable Excel workbooks on the Previous Rates page: 'Historical Rates Revised Rule' (covering 2021-04-01 forward, the current national-rate definition) and 'Historical Rates Prior Rule' (covering 2009-05-18 to the 2021-04-01 rule change, an earlier definition of national rate/rate cap). The Prior Rule and Revised Rule figures are not the same methodology and should not be spliced without noting the break.

Every national-rate/national-rate-cap series is also hosted on FRED (see datasets[].access.via below), but FRED only carries the Revised Rule period (2021-04-01 onward) — the Prior Rule (2009-05-18 to 2021-03-01) exists only in the FDIC's own Excel workbook.

terms.summary: No explicit copyright or public-domain statement for FDIC's own website content; the site's general disclaimer addresses only third-party linked sites ("External sites may contain information that is copyrighted with restrictions on reuse. Permission to use copyrighted materials must be obtained from the original source and cannot be obtained from the FDIC.") and makes no reuse statement about FDIC's own data

datasets.name: National Rates and Rate Caps
datasets.gives: Monthly national average deposit rate ("national rate") and the corresponding national rate cap, for savings, interest checking, money market, and CDs at 1/3/6/12/24/36/48/60-month terms — 9 products x 2 (rate, cap) = 18 series. Also hosted on FRED (revised-rule period only): SNDR/SNRC (savings), ICNDR/ICNRC (interest checking), MMNDR/MMNRC (money market), NDR1MCD/NRC1MCD, NDR3MCD/NRC3MCD, NDR6MCD/NRC6MCD, NDR12MCD/NRC12MCD, NDR24MCD/NRC24MCD, NDR36MCD/NRC36MCD (rate only — FRED had no NRC36MCD as of 2026-09-15), NDR48MCD/NRC48MCD, NDR60MCD/NRC60MCD (via: fred).
notes: The 'national rate' is defined (FDIC, effective 2021-04-01) as the average of rates paid by all insured depository institutions and credit unions for which data is available, weighted by each institution's share of domestic deposits — a deposit-weighted average of rates actually paid on retail accounts, not a survey of the highest advertised or brokered CD offers.
Savings and interest checking rates use the $2,500 product tier; money market and CD rates are an average of the $10,000 and $100,000 product tiers.
Underlying bank-level data source is S&P Capital IQ Pro and SNL Financial Data; the FDIC does the rate/cap calculation itself.

The 'national rate cap' is the higher of (national rate + 75bp) or (120% of the similar-maturity U.S. Treasury yield + 75bp); for savings/interest checking/money market (non-maturity products) it is the higher of (national rate + 75bp) or (federal funds rate + 75bp).

Publication schedule: the 3rd Monday of each month (next business day if that Monday is a Federal holiday); FDIC does not state a fixed publication lag in business days relative to the reference month-end.

A rule change effective 2021-04-01 redefined both 'national rate' and 'national rate cap'; the FDIC's own historical workbooks split at that date ('Prior Rule' vs 'Revised Rule') and FRED hosts only the Revised Rule period.
CDs published are 'on-tenor' maturities (1/3/6/12/24/36/48/60 months); an off-tenor CD (e.g. 26-month) uses the next-shorter on-tenor rate per FDIC's own rule text.
